lessons.title: Le printemps arrive - premiers signes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe and identify the first signs that spring is beginning in our environment

opening.activity: Circle time (8 min): Show winter photo of school yard from earlier this year. Ask 'Qu'est-ce qui est différent maintenant?' Look out window together. Point and name: 'C'est le printemps!' Teach spring gesture (arms opening like flowers).

main.activity: Spring detective walk (27 min): Outdoor exploration with clipboards and spring signs checklist. Students search for: warmer air (feel with hands), longer daylight (discuss morning/evening), buds on trees, birds singing, people wearing lighter clothes. Each student draws 2-3 spring signs they find. Practice saying 'Au printemps, je vois...' Create class spring discovery chart with student findings.

closing.activity: Science circle (10 min): Students share one spring sign they discovered. Teacher records on class chart with simple drawings. End with spring awakening chant: 'Le printemps arrive, tout se réveille!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize spring changes they see walking to school or playing outside with families

lessons.title: Les bourgeons réveillent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe buds on trees and understand that plants are waking up from winter rest

opening.activity: Connection to previous lesson (8 min): Review spring signs from Lesson 1. Today we're looking closer at trees. Show sleeping gesture: 'En hiver, les arbres dorment.' Then waking up gesture: 'Au printemps, ils se réveillent!' Introduce 'bourgeons' with hand motions.

main.activity: Tree awakening exploration (27 min): Outdoor investigation focusing on tree branches and buds. Students work in pairs to find different types of buds using observation sheets. Use magnifying glasses to examine bud shapes, colors, and sizes. Practice vocabulary: 'Je vois des bourgeons sur les branches.' Students draw their favorite buds and predict what will happen next. Create class bud observation journal with student drawings and predictions.

closing.activity: Bud discovery sharing (10 min): Students show their bud drawings and share predictions. Teacher introduces concept: 'Les bourgeons vont devenir des feuilles!' End with tree awakening movement: arms as branches, hands as buds slowly opening.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice buds on trees in their neighborhoods and understand trees are getting ready to grow

lessons.title: Pourquoi les plantes se réveillent-elles?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that plants wake up in spring because they get more sun and warmth

opening.activity: Connecting to buds (8 min): Review buds from Lesson 2. Ask 'Pourquoi les bourgeons se réveillent maintenant?' Introduce sun and warmth concepts with gestures: sun rays (arms spreading), warmth (hugging self), plant growth (growing taller).

main.activity: Plant needs investigation (27 min): Dramatic exploration of plant needs using movement and props. Students act as sleeping plants (curled up), then teacher adds 'sun' (flashlight) and 'warmth' (warm air from heater), and plants 'wake up' and grow. Set up simple experiment: place identical plants in warm sunny spot vs. cool dark spot. Students predict what will happen. Create plant needs chart with drawings of sun, warmth, and growing plants. Practice saying 'Les plantes ont besoin de soleil et de chaleur.'

closing.activity: Plant needs review (10 min): Students demonstrate plant awakening sequence with movements. Review plant needs chart together. End with plant awakening song: 'Soleil, chaleur, les plantes poussent!'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand why their family gardens start growing when weather gets warmer in spring

lessons.title: Les premières feuilles vertes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe the emergence of new green leaves and understand this shows healthy plant growth

opening.activity: Building on plant growth (8 min): Review how sun and warmth help plants grow from Lesson 3. Today we'll see what happens to buds! Show sequence: bud → small leaf → bigger leaf. Use hand gestures to show leaf unfurling from closed fist to open hand.

main.activity: New leaf discovery walk (27 min): Outdoor leaf investigation focusing on brand-new spring growth. Students search for the tiniest new leaves and the brightest green colors. Use simple leaf observation sheets to draw different leaf shapes and sizes. Count new leaves on chosen branches. Practice vocabulary: 'Je vois de nouvelles feuilles vertes.' Compare new spring leaves with old ones still on trees. Create class leaf collection (draw, don't pick) showing variety of new spring growth.

closing.activity: Leaf growth celebration (10 min): Students share their favorite new leaf discoveries. Discuss how new leaves show plants are healthy and growing. End with leaf growing movement: start as tiny buds, slowly unfurl into full leaves reaching toward the sun.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice new green leaves appearing on trees and plants around their homes and playgrounds

lessons.title: Il fait plus chaud - mesurer le printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe that spring brings warmer temperatures and learn to measure temperature changes

opening.activity: Connection to warmth (8 min): Review how plants need warmth from Lesson 3. Ask students to feel the air temperature with their skin. Introduce thermometer as a tool that 'tells us how warm or cold it is.' Show thermometer and demonstrate reading it together.

main.activity: Temperature investigation (27 min): Outdoor temperature exploration using classroom thermometer. Students take turns reading the thermometer in different locations: sunny spots, shady areas, near building, in open space. Record temperatures on simple chart using pictures (sun for warm, snowflake for cold). Practice vocabulary: 'Il fait plus chaud aujourd'hui.' Compare current spring temperature to winter temperature from earlier in year. Students draw pictures showing how temperature affects their clothing choices and activities.

closing.activity: Temperature discoveries (10 min): Review temperature findings from different locations. Discuss why some spots are warmer than others. End with temperature movement: huddle together for cold, spread out with arms up for warm.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand how families check weather temperature to decide what clothes to wear

lessons.title: Les jours deviennent plus longs
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe that daylight hours increase in spring and understand how this affects living things

opening.activity: Building on temperature (8 min): Review warmer spring temperatures from Lesson 5. Introduce new concept: spring days are also longer! Ask students if they notice staying up later or getting up when it's lighter. Show window and discuss how much light we see.

main.activity: Daylight exploration (27 min): Indoor and outdoor investigation of daily light changes. Students observe light coming through classroom windows at different times if possible. Go outside to notice how bright it is and compare to students' memories of winter darkness. Create simple timeline showing winter short days vs. spring longer days using pictures. Practice vocabulary: 'Les jours sont plus longs au printemps.' Discuss how longer light affects plants (more growing time) and animals (more time to find food and be active).

closing.activity: Long day celebration (10 min): Students share what they like about longer spring days. Create class list of spring day activities that weren't possible in short winter days. End with day length movement: short winter day (small, curled up) growing into long spring day (arms stretched wide).

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize they can play outside later and families don't turn lights on as early

lessons.title: Les animaux se réveillent aussi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe how animals become more active in spring as they emerge from winter rest

opening.activity: Connecting to longer days (8 min): Review longer spring days from Lesson 6. Introduce new idea: animals also notice spring changes! Ask students if they've seen more birds, insects, or other animals lately. Use movement to show sleepy winter animals waking up.

main.activity: Spring animal observation (27 min): Outdoor animal activity investigation. Students work in pairs to observe and record animal signs: bird sounds, insect movements, animal tracks, evidence of animal activity. Use simple animal observation sheets with pictures to identify common spring animals. Practice vocabulary: 'Les animaux sont plus actifs.' Create class animal activity chart showing what animals do differently in spring vs. winter. Discuss why animals are more active (warmer weather, more food, longer days).

closing.activity: Animal awakening sharing (10 min): Students demonstrate animal movements they observed or imagined. Share findings from animal activity chart. End with animal awakening sequence: hibernate (sleep), feel warmth (stretch), become active (move around).

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students notice more birds singing, bees buzzing, and animals moving around their neighborhoods

lessons.title: Les oiseaux construisent des nids
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that spring is nesting season and observe bird nest-building behaviors

opening.activity: Building on animal activity (8 min): Review how animals are more active in spring from Lesson 7. Focus on birds today. Ask if students have noticed birds carrying sticks or grass. Introduce concept: birds build nests in spring! Use hand motions to show building/weaving actions.

main.activity: Bird nesting investigation (27 min): Outdoor bird and nest observation focusing on nesting behaviors and materials. Students look for: birds carrying materials, existing nests in trees (from safe distance), nest-building materials on ground. Use bird behavior observation sheets to record what they see. Practice vocabulary: 'Les oiseaux construisent des nids.' Collect fallen nest materials (twigs, grass, feathers) to examine how birds build homes. Create classroom display of nest materials and discuss why birds choose different materials.

closing.activity: Nest building understanding (10 min): Students examine collected nest materials and discuss how birds use them. Share observations of bird behaviors. End with bird nest building movements: gathering materials (picking up), carrying (walking with arms full), building (weaving motions).

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand why they see birds carrying sticks and building nests in trees around their homes

lessons.title: Pourquoi faire des nids au printemps?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that animals make nests in spring to prepare for their babies

opening.activity: Connecting to nest building (8 min): Review bird nest building from Lesson 8. Ask students why they think birds work so hard to build nests. Introduce concept: nests are homes for baby birds! Use caring gestures to show protection and safety.

main.activity: Animal family exploration (27 min): Investigation of how animals prepare homes for babies using pictures, videos, and discussion. Students look at photos of baby birds in nests, discuss why babies need protection. Compare animal families to human families - both need safe homes. Practice vocabulary: 'Les parents protègent leurs bébés.' Create class book about animal families showing different animals and their babies in spring homes. Students draw pictures of animal families being safe and cared for.

closing.activity: Family care understanding (10 min): Students share their animal family drawings and explain how parents take care of babies. Review why spring is good time for animal babies (warm weather, lots of food). End with family care movements: building safe home, feeding babies, keeping them warm.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand that both animal families and human families work to keep their babies safe and cared for

lessons.title: Expérience: faire pousser des graines
lessons.oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments to grow seeds and understand how plants begin life in spring

opening.activity: Connecting to plant growth (8 min): Review how plants need sun and warmth from earlier lessons. Introduce new concept: plants start from tiny seeds! Show various seeds and ask students to predict what they might grow into.

main.activity: Seed planting experiment (27 min): Hands-on seed planting investigation where students plant seeds and set up growth experiment. Each student plants 2-3 seeds in small pots with soil and water. Set up controlled experiment: some seeds with water, some without; some in light, some in dark. Students make predictions about which seeds will grow best. Practice vocabulary: 'Je plante des graines dans la terre.' Create seed growth tracking charts where students will draw daily observations. Discuss what seeds need to grow (water, soil, warmth, light).

closing.activity: Seed experiment setup (10 min): Students explain their predictions about which seeds will grow best. Review what seeds need to grow. End with seed growth movement: start curled up like seed, slowly grow with water and sun until tall plant.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand how gardens and farms start with tiny seeds that grow into food and flowers

lessons.title: Les fleurs apparaissent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe spring flowers and understand they help plants make new seeds

opening.activity: Building on plant growth (8 min): Check seed experiment from Lesson 10 and celebrate any sprouting. Introduce today's focus: flowers are appearing on plants outside! Ask students what flowers they've noticed. Show examples of spring flowers.

main.activity: Spring flower investigation (27 min): Outdoor flower observation and exploration focusing on spring blooms. Students use flower observation sheets to record colors, shapes, sizes, and scents of different flowers. Practice vocabulary: 'Je vois des fleurs colorées.' Use magnifying glasses to examine flower parts up close. Students create flower color wheel showing all the spring flower colors they find. Discuss why flowers are colorful and smell nice (to attract insects). Gentle flower touching and smelling activities (with safe flowers only).

closing.activity: Flower beauty celebration (10 min): Students share their favorite flower discoveries and explain why they liked them. Show flower color wheel and discuss variety of spring flowers. End with flower blooming movement: start as closed bud, slowly open into beautiful flower with arms as petals.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students enjoy the beautiful flowers that bloom in gardens, parks, and wild areas during springtime

lessons.title: Les insectes reviennent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe that insects become active in spring and understand their connection to flowers

opening.activity: Connecting flowers to insects (8 min): Review beautiful spring flowers from Lesson 11. Ask students if they've noticed any small flying creatures near flowers. Introduce concept: insects love flowers! Show pictures of bees, butterflies, and other spring insects.

main.activity: Spring insect observation (27 min): Outdoor insect investigation focusing on beneficial insects and their relationship with flowers. Students observe insects from safe distance using insect observation sheets. Practice vocabulary: 'Les insectes visitent les fleurs.' Look for bees on flowers, butterflies flying around, other insects in spring environment. Create class chart showing which insects visit which flowers. Discuss why insects like flowers (nectar for food) and how this helps plants (insects carry pollen). Simple movement activity: students act as flowers, others as visiting insects.

closing.activity: Insect-flower connection understanding (10 min): Students share their insect observations and demonstrate insect movements they saw. Review how insects and flowers help each other. End with pollination dance: flower students stand still, insect students visit flowers and 'collect nectar.'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand why they see bees and butterflies around flowers in their gardens and neighborhoods

lessons.title: Notre jardin de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan and start a spring garden to observe plant growth throughout the season

opening.activity: Culminating plant learning (8 min): Review all plant learning from previous lessons: seeds growing, plants needing warmth and sun, flowers appearing. Introduce exciting project: creating our own class spring garden! Show examples of spring gardens and discuss what we might grow.

main.activity: Spring garden planning and planting (27 min): Collaborative garden creation project applying all spring plant learning. Students help choose what to plant, prepare soil, plant seeds or seedlings, and set up garden care system. Practice vocabulary: 'Nous créons notre jardin de printemps.' Each student has a role in garden setup. Create garden care calendar showing when to water, observe, and tend plants. Students make predictions about how garden will change over time. Set up garden observation journals for ongoing documentation.

closing.activity: Garden commitment ceremony (10 min): Students make commitment to care for class garden throughout spring. Explain how garden will help us continue learning about spring plant growth. End with garden care pledge and movements showing different garden care activities.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students experience how families grow their own food and flowers in home gardens

lessons.title: Notre livre scientifique de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a class science book documenting all their spring observations and discoveries

opening.activity: Celebrating spring learning (8 min): Review all the amazing spring discoveries from Lessons 1-13. Show students their accumulated work: observation sheets, drawings, garden journals. Announce special project: creating a book about our spring science journey!

main.activity: Spring science book creation (27 min): Collaborative documentation project synthesizing all spring learning into class book. Students organize their drawings, observations, and discoveries into book sections: spring signs, plant growth, animal activity, flowers and insects, our garden. Practice vocabulary: 'Nous documentons nos découvertes.' Students contribute pages showing their best spring observations with drawings and simple captions. Create book sections for: what we learned about spring weather, plant changes, animal behaviors, experiments we did. Students practice presenting their pages to classmates.

closing.activity: Book completion celebration (10 min): Students share favorite pages from spring science book. Discuss how their book shows all the amazing things they learned about spring. Plan to share book with families or other classes. End with proud scientist celebration dance.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand how scientists document and share their discoveries to help others learn about nature

lessons.title: Prédictions: que va-t-il se passer en été?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use their spring observations to make scientific predictions about summer changes (extension)

opening.activity: Transitioning to summer thinking (8 min): Review spring science book from Lesson 14. Ask students what they think will happen as spring continues into summer. Show calendar indicating progression of seasons. Introduce prediction concept with simple examples.

main.activity: Summer prediction investigation (27 min): Extension activity using spring learning to predict summer changes. Students use their spring observations to make logical predictions about summer: Will it get even warmer? Will plants grow bigger? What will happen to our garden? Practice vocabulary: 'Je prédis qu'en été...' Create prediction charts for weather, plants, and animals based on spring patterns observed. Students draw pictures showing their summer predictions. Discuss what evidence from spring supports their predictions.

closing.activity: Prediction sharing and planning (10 min): Students present their summer predictions with reasoning. Plan how they might test their predictions over the summer. End with future scientist excitement about continuing observations.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students practice thinking like scientists by using evidence to predict future natural changes

lessons.title: Printemps autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how spring looks different in various climates and regions (extension)

opening.activity: Expanding spring perspective (8 min): Review local spring observations from all previous lessons. Introduce concept: spring happens all around the world, but looks different in different places! Show globe and indicate different locations where spring occurs.

main.activity: World spring exploration (27 min): Extension investigation of global spring variations using photos, videos, and simple maps. Students observe photos of spring in different climates: desert spring, tropical spring, arctic spring, mountain spring. Practice vocabulary: 'Le printemps est différent partout dans le monde.' Compare similarities and differences to local spring observations. Create world spring display showing how spring plants, animals, and weather vary globally. Students choose favorite global spring example to draw and explain.

closing.activity: Global spring appreciation (10 min): Students share their favorite examples of spring around the world. Discuss similarities in spring changes everywhere (warming, growing, animal activity). End with world spring celebration representing different global spring examples.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students understand that children around the world experience spring differently but share similar natural changes

lessons.title: Expérience: créer des conditions de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will design experiments to recreate spring conditions and observe their effects (extension)

opening.activity: Connecting to spring conditions (8 min): Review all spring conditions learned: warmth, longer light, more water from spring rains. Challenge students: Can we create spring conditions inside to see what happens?

main.activity: Spring conditions experiment design (27 min): Advanced extension activity where students design experiments to test spring conditions. Students set up controlled experiments: plants with extra warmth vs. normal temperature, plants with extra light vs. normal light, plants with spring-like watering vs. winter-like watering. Practice vocabulary: 'Nous créons des expériences.' Students make predictions about results and set up observation schedules. Create experiment recording sheets to track changes over time. Discuss experimental design concepts appropriate for Grade 1.

closing.activity: Experiment launch celebration (10 min): Students explain their experiment designs and predictions. Plan ongoing observation schedule. End with scientist excitement about discovering results.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students learn how scientists use controlled experiments to understand how environmental conditions affect living things

lessons.title: Le printemps et les humains
lessons.oneGoal: Students will investigate how humans adapt their behaviors and activities for spring changes (extension)

opening.activity: Connecting to human behavior (8 min): Review animal spring behaviors from previous lessons. Ask students how people change their behavior in spring too. Start with obvious examples like clothing and outdoor activities.

main.activity: Human spring adaptation investigation (27 min): Extension exploration of how humans respond to spring changes through behavioral adaptations. Students investigate human spring changes: lighter clothing, more outdoor activities, spring cleaning, gardening, different foods. Practice vocabulary: 'Les humains s'adaptent au printemps.' Compare human and animal spring behaviors: both become more active, both prepare homes (animals build nests, humans do spring cleaning), both take advantage of better weather. Create comparison chart showing human vs. animal spring adaptations. Students interview each other about family spring traditions and changes.

closing.activity: Human-animal spring connection (10 min): Students share family spring traditions and compare to animal behaviors. Celebrate similarities between human and animal responses to spring. End with adaptation movement showing both human and animal spring activities.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students recognize that their families adapt to spring just like animals do, changing activities and behaviors for the season

lessons.title: Présentation scientifique de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will present their spring science discoveries to others using scientific language and evidence (extension)

opening.activity: Preparing to share learning (8 min): Review all spring science learning from throughout the unit. Explain that scientists share their discoveries with others. Today students become spring science presenters!

main.activity: Spring science presentation preparation and delivery (27 min): Culminating extension activity where students prepare and deliver presentations about spring science learning. Students choose their best spring discovery to share: plant growth experiments, animal observations, weather measurements, garden progress, or other spring learning. Practice vocabulary: 'Je présente mes découvertes scientifiques.' Students prepare simple presentations using drawings, photos, or actual materials as evidence. Practice presenting to small groups first, then to whole class. Include question and answer sessions after each presentation.

closing.activity: Presentation celebration (10 min): Celebrate all student presentations and scientific communication growth. Discuss what made presentations effective. End with proud scientist applause for everyone's spring discoveries.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students practice important communication skills that scientists use to share discoveries with other people

lessons.title: Fête des petits scientifiques de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their spring science journey with families by sharing experiments and discoveries (extension)

opening.activity: Celebration preparation (8 min): Review entire spring science journey with students. Explain that they will share their learning with families. Assign roles and practice celebration activities.

main.activity: Spring science celebration event (27 min): Culminating extension celebration where students showcase spring science learning to families and community. Students lead families through learning stations: spring observation displays, plant growth demonstrations, garden tours, science book sharing, animal behavior explanations, weather measurement activities. Practice vocabulary: 'Nous célébrons nos découvertes scientifiques.' Students act as science guides explaining their discoveries to visitors. Include hands-on activities families can try together. Display all student work and accomplishments from the unit.

closing.activity: Celebration wrap-up and reflection (10 min): Thank families for participating. Students reflect on their favorite spring science discoveries. End with group celebration of becoming spring scientists and commitment to continue observing nature.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Students experience the joy of sharing scientific discoveries with their families and build community connections around learning

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en sciences
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Le printemps arrive - premiers signes, Les bourgeons réveillent, Pourquoi les plantes se réveillent-elles?, Les premières feuilles vertes, Il fait plus chaud - mesurer le printemps

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Encouragez les questions 'pourquoi' et explorez ensemble les réponses.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

La curiosité scientifique commence à la maison!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
